name: Idiosyncratic gap-down fade, flat market days
hypothesis: The 1% gap fade (gross -1.1 bps) and the deep VWAP stretch (losses concentrated on market-wide down days, where many names fall together) failed because a gap in many stocks at once is macro news that keeps going. A 1.5% gap in one large cap while the universe's median gap is within 0.3% is more likely an overnight order imbalance in a thin pre-market than information, so the retracement as regular-session liquidity arrives should be larger and independent across names. Written before any run. Expected to fail if single-name gaps of that size are mostly earnings and guidance, which drift on rather than revert; then the 1.5% stop dominates, as before.
